content: Differences from innerHTML: Element.innerHTML gets or sets HTML, as its name indicates. We advise against using innerHTML to get or set text inside an element because it deals with raw HTML rather than plain text and can be susceptible to XSS attacks . Even if you are sure that the text never contains HTML syntax, it is still less semantic and slower because it needs to invoke the HTML parser. Setting textContent on a node removes all of the node's children and replaces them with a single text node with the given string value.
conclusion: Node.textContent replaces children with a single text node without invoking HTML parser, preventing XSS attacks.
